title: Properties and Chemical Reactions
seo_title: Grade 7 Chemical Reactions Worksheets: Characteristic Properties and Evidence of a Reaction
standard_text: Analyze and interpret data on the properties of substances before and after the substances interact to determine if a chemical reaction has occurred.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on properties and chemical reactions (NGSS MS-PS1-2): characteristic properties like density and melting point, chemical vs. physical changes, and before-and-after data. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: New properties mean a new substance.
key_sub: Compare density, melting point and other characteristic properties before and after. If they change, a chemical reaction happened.
body_html:
How to think about it

Every pure substance has characteristic properties that do not depend on how much you have: density, melting point, boiling point, solubility, flammability and odor.

In a chemical reaction, atoms rearrange to form new substances, so the characteristic properties change. Evidence: a gas forms, a solid forms from liquids, the color changes, the temperature changes, light is given off, or there is a new smell.

In a physical change (melting, boiling, dissolving, cutting, bending), the substance stays the same. Compare properties before and after to decide.

Example

An iron nail becomes orange-brown and is no longer magnetic. Chemical or physical?

Its properties changed.

A new substance (rust) formed.

Answer: chemical

Example

Ice melts into water. Chemical or physical?

It is still water.

Answer: physical

Common mistakes

  • Thinking melting or boiling is a chemical reaction.
  • Thinking dissolving makes a new substance.
  • Using mass or volume to identify a substance. Use characteristic properties.

faq.q: How can you tell if a chemical reaction happened?
faq.a: Compare characteristic properties before and after. Signs include a new gas, a new solid, a color or temperature change, light or a new smell.
Properties that do not depend on the amount, such as density, melting point, boiling point, solubility and flammability.

faq.q: Is dissolving sugar in water a chemical reaction?
faq.a: No. The sugar is still there and comes back when the water evaporates, so it is a physical change.

items.e: The substance is still the same; only its shape, size or state changed.

items.e: Density = mass ÷ volume.
